# Step 53: 3½" wire from eyelet #7 (S) to left RCA long lug

> *Connect one end of a 3 ½" wire to eyelet #7 (S). Connect the other end to the (long) lug of the left input socket.* — manual page 9

## What you're doing physically

A 3½" wire from PC-3 eyelet #7 to the long lug of the left RCA. The eyelet end is soldered (S); the RCA end is NOT yet — more wires land there in step 54.

## What this carries

Eyelet #7 is the **left channel signal input** on the PC-3 board. Same role as eyelet #17 for the right channel.

## Why longer than step 52

Step 52's right-channel wire was 1¾"; this left-channel wire is 3½". The asymmetry is because the PC-3 board's input pads are not centred — they're closer to one side of the chassis. Hence one channel's input wire is shorter than the other's.

The longer wire is fine — it's still short enough not to pick up significant hum, especially since the input switch and surrounding chassis provide partial shielding.
